GitHub Enterprise and the Ledgerline Admin Console are also Okta-assigned applications.

questions.question: Is all customer data encrypted at rest? Specify the algorithm and how keys are managed.
questions.answer: Yes. Customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. The production PostgreSQL database (Amazon RDS) and the S3 buckets holding customer statement files and reconciliation exports are encrypted with a customer-managed AWS KMS key that rotates automatically every year. Reconciliation export files created before 2026-11-07 remain encrypted with AES-256 under S3-managed keys until they expire, no later than 2026-12-07.

history.note: CONTRADICTION. RDS (rds.tf:7-8), statements bucket (s3.tf:6-13), audit logs (logging.tf:25-33) use the KMS CMK. recon_exports bucket (s3.tf:26-28, added 2026-05, customer transaction reports) has no SSE configuration, so it is on S3-managed default keys, not the CMK. Policy information-security-policy.md:10-11 says every bucket. Need: fix now (add SSE-KMS block) or disclose.
Fixed: SSE-KMS block added to recon_exports (s3.tf:30-38), diff approved by Dev in ~infra 09:35. Existing objects stay SSE-S3 until 30-day expiry (s3.tf:53).

Checked all production customer-data stores: RDS uses storage_encrypted = true and aws_kms_key.data; both customer S3 buckets have aws:kms SSE on that key. Existing export objects remain under prior encryption until the enabled 30-day lifecycle expiration, hence at most 30 days after 2026-11-07. No other customer-data bucket or database resource found.

questions.question: Is customer data encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher?
questions.answer: Yes, for customer traffic over public networks. The public API load balancer serves HTTPS using AWS security policy ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06 (TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred). Plain HTTP requests on port 80 are redirected to HTTPS with a 301.

history.note: Scoped to public networks: internal hops (ALB to app, app to RDS) aren't provable from company/.
Checked HTTPS listener, TLS policy and HTTP redirect; configured minimum is TLS 1.2 as stated.

questions.question: Are encryption keys rotated automatically?
questions.answer: Yes. The customer-managed AWS KMS key (alias/ledgerline-data) used for the production database, the customer statements bucket, the audit log bucket and Secrets Manager has automatic key rotation enabled; AWS KMS rotates the key material annually. The production database credential is rotated automatically every 30 days.

history.note: Checked KMS key rotation plus encryption configuration for RDS, statements and audit logs and the Secrets Manager secrets; named resources match the answer.

questions.question: Are databases holding customer data isolated from the public internet?
questions.answer: Yes. The production PostgreSQL database (Amazon RDS) is not publicly accessible and runs in private subnets. Its security group accepts connections on port 5432 only from the application tier's security group.

history.note: Checked RDS public accessibility, private subnet group and DB security group ingress; database is private and accepts 5432 only from app tier.

questions.question: How are application secrets and credentials stored and rotated?
questions.answer: Application secrets and credentials are stored in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypted with Ledgerline's customer-managed AWS KMS key. The production database credential is rotated automatically every 30 days by a Secrets Manager rotation function. Third-party API keys held in Secrets Manager do not have automatic rotation configured.

history.note: Checked Secrets Manager resources and rotation config; database rotates every 30 days, LLM key is stored there, and answer explicitly says third-party keys do not auto-rotate.

questions.answer: Yes.
